## QUESTION 1 [20]

A wildlife biologist examines frogs for a genetic trait he suspects may be linked to sensitivity to industrial toxins in the environment. Previous research had established that this trait is usually found in 1 of every 8 frogs. He collects and examines a dozen frogs. If the frequency of the trait has not changed, what's the probability that he finds the trait in...

### 1A [5]

**None of the 12 frogs?**

```{r}
dbinom(0, 12, 0.125)

```

**ANSWER:** 0.2014172

### 1B [5]

**At least 2 frogs?**

```{r}
1 - pbinom(1, size = 12, prob = 0.125)

```

**ANSWER:** 0.4532961

### 1C [5]

**3 or 4 frogs?**

```{r}
dbinom(4, 12, 0.125)+dbinom(3,12, 0.125)

```

**ANSWER:** 0.1707139

### 1D [5]

**no more than 4 frogs?**

```{r}
pbinom(4, size=12 ,prob=0.372)

```

**ANSWER:**  0.5190417

## QUESTION 2 [30]

![](images/clipboard-2859136471.png)

A sporting goods store announces a “Wheel of Savings” sale. Customers select the merchandise they want to purchase, then at the cash register they spin a wheel (pictured above) to determine the size of the discount they will receive. The wheel is divided into 12 regions, like a clock. Six of those regions are red and award a 10% discount. The three white regions award a 20% discount and two blue regions a 40% discount. The remaining region is gold, and a customer whose lucky spin lands there gets a 100% discount—the merchandise is free!

### 2A [5]

What is the probability that a customer gets at least a 40% discount?

```{r}
(2+1)/12

```

**ANSWER:** 0.25

### 2B [5]

What is the probability that two customers in a row get only 10% discounts?

```{r}
(6/12)*(6/12)

```

**ANSWER:** 0.25

### 2C [5]

What is the probability that three consecutive customers all get 20% discounts?

```{r}
(3/12)*(3/12)*(3/12)

```

**ANSWER:** 0.015625

### 2D [5]

What is the probability that none of the first four customers gets a discount over 20%?

```{r}
(9/12)^4

```

**ANSWER:** 0.3164062

### 2E [5]

What is the probability that the first gold winner (100%) is the fifth customer in line?

```{r}
(11/12)^4*(1/12)

```

**ANSWER:**  0.0588389

### 2F [5]

What is the probability that there is at least one gold winner among the first six customers?

```{r}
1 - (11/12)^6

```

**ANSWER:** 0.4067078
